text: The centre and its strategical significance

text: The knight on e5 and d5 (e4 and d4). The pawn centre. Attack with the central "hanging" pawns.

text: The part of the board which includes the squares e4, d4, e5 and d5 is called the centre. These squares are called central.

text: The arrangement of the pieces in the centre, from where they operate e in several directions, might serve as a basis for the construction of very active plans. Many different ideas and combinations have been carried out on this basis.
zh: 棋子配置在中心后可以向多个方向发挥作用，这可成为制定积极计划的基础。许多不同的构想与组合都建立在这一基础上。

text: Athe end of the last century the famous American chessplayer, Pillsbury, was able to win a number of interesting games where the basis of the initiative was the planting of a knight on e5. In the 20's and 30's of our century, a plan, where the whole object was the occupation of the d5 square (for Black - d4) with the knight, became increasingly pronounced. The centralised knight, supported by pawns, hampered the activity of the opponent, guaranteed a lasting initiative and frequently broughthe champions of such ideas success.
zh: 十九世纪末，美国名将皮尔斯伯里赢下了多盘精彩对局；他取得主动的基础，正是把马安置在e5。到了二十世纪二三十年代，以马占据d5（黑方则为d4）为全部目标的计划愈发常见。得到兵支持的中心马能够限制对手棋子的活动，保证持久的主动权，并屡屡为这一构想的拥护者带来成功。

text: Two central pawns, standing side by side, hold under their influence four squares on the next rank. The advance of the pawn centre sometimes causes real disarray in the enemy camp, particularly when a counterattack against such a breakthrough group proves unsuccessful. The pawn centre gains in strength when there is harmony between it and the pieceforces. text: When the pawn centre advances, it loses touch with its own rear and draws closer to the superior strength of the opponent. zh: 黑方有可能以或多或少合理的棋局转移到中央舞台，但他需要对他所面临的问题有很好的理解。事实是，在将黑方棋子从d5移走后，白方威胁要建立一个兵中心。S. 塔拉什甚至认为此举2... dxc4是中心的投降，并总是给它打一个问号。然而，这种评价是教条式的。黑方有很多方法可以阻止前进e4，实际上d4棋子的位置也不是绝对稳定的，考虑到可能出现的断点...c5和...e5。当然，答复2... c6或2... e6，巩固d5兵，有利于黑方在中间的斗争，但导致棋局相对平静，难以获得反击机会。然而，此举2... dxc4使得斗争更加激烈。在接受该策略后产生的紧张局势中，黑方可以利用许多组合图案。因此，如果白方现在直接下兵中心 3. e4，那么鉴于

text: reply 3... e5 (4. dxe5 Qxd1+ 5. Kxd1 Be6 and then... Nc6 with hopes of seizing the initiative). On 3. Nc3, in the game Capablanca-I. Rabinovich (Moscow 1925) Black replied 3... a6 and after 4. a4 e5! obtained a position with excellent prospects. 3. Nf3 Nf6
zh: 回复3... e5（4dxe5Qxd1+5Kxd1Be6然后...Nc6希望能抢占先机）。在 3. Nc3 上，对局 卡帕布兰卡-I 中。Rabinovich (莫斯科 1925) Black 回复 3... a6，4 后 a4 e5! 获得了前景良好的位置。3. Nf3 Nf6

zh: 终于！

text: Black's position is not easy. White has built up a pawn centre and a mobile one at that, as a consequence of which his piecearmy also threatens to advance. Black lags behind seriously in development (this is also not surprising, since, out of his first ten moves, he has made five with the knight), his king is detained in the centre - it all foreshadows an impending denouement.
zh: 黑方的处境并不容易。白方已经建立了一个兵中心和一个移动中心，因此他的零散子力也有前进的威胁。黑方在发展上严重落后（这也不足为奇，因为在他的前十步中，他已经与马下了五步），他的王被困在中间 - 这一切都预示着即将到来的结局。

text: The question, as to whether he should hurry with the opening of the game or continue to systematically increase the pressure resulting from the pawn centre, presents itself a a purely 1 strategical problem. Both plans are justified and the choice of one of them, in the present position, depends more on the style and creative direction of the chessplayer.
zh: 至于他是应该尽快开局还是继续有系统地增加兵中心的压力，这本身就是一个纯粹的战略问题。两种方案都有道理，在目前情况下选择其中一种，更多地取决于棋手的风格和创作方向。

text: And White's advantage is quite obvious. Admittedly, the process of realisation still requires quite a long time.
zh: 而白方的优势也是相当明显的。诚然，实现的过程还需要相当长的时间。

zh: 一个有趣的时刻。如果我们将这次交流视为一次单独的战术行动，那么它应该受到谴责。这也引起了棋评人士的批评，认为黑方一是加强了白方中央的o组，使白方更容易形成兵中，二是打开了b线，从而增加了白方在后翼的活跃可能性。

text: But nevertheless these considerations do not give grounds to criticise e the exchange made by Black, which in fact is a very important link in his contemplated plan. Relyin on the pawn tension "d4-c5" (pawn tension - is an arrangement t of pawns whereby they attack each other), Black intended to concentrate the action of his heavy pieces on the c-file, and then, by takin on d4 at a suitable moment, to begin active play on this file. lt is unfavourable for White to eliminate the tension himself by dxc5, since after this
zh: 但尽管如此，这些考虑并没有成为批评黑方所做的交换的理由，这实际上是他所设想的计划中非常重要的一环。依靠棋子张力“d4-c5”（棋子张力 - 棋子相互攻击的排列方式），黑方打算将重子的动作集中在 c 线上，然后在适当的时刻吃 d4，开始在此线上积极下棋。白方通过dxc5自行消除紧张是不利的，因为此后

text: not it is a link in the plan and only then to look at its indefinite tactical significance for the given position.
zh: 不是计划中的一个环节，然后才考虑其对于给定位置的不确定的战术意义。

text: White claims his right to the centre, buthe advance 11. d5, for the present, is not dangerous for Black. On this follows 1l... e5, and the action of White's king's bishop will be limited by its own pawn chain. True, White obtains a well consolidated passed pawn in the centre, but Black's pieces (particularly the knight) can blockade it effectively from the d6 square, athe same time exerting strong pressure on the opponent's position. However, White is not obliged to play d5. He has formed a pawn centre and under its cover could strive to create more active play on one of the flanks. To counterbalance this, Black must try to organise an attack on the c-file.
zh: 白方声称拥有中间的权利，但目前前进 11. d5 对黑方来说并不危险。接下来是 1l...e5，白方王的象的行动将受到其自己的兵链的限制。诚然，白方在中心获得了一个巩固的传棋，但黑方的棋子（特别是马）可以从d6格中有效地封锁它，同时对对手的位置施加强大的压力。然而，白方没有义务下d5。他已经组建了一个兵中心，并在其掩护下努力在一侧创造更积极的对局。为了平衡这一点，黑方必须尝试组织对c线的进攻。

zh: Qc7，以免象在f4上发展。同时，动后将有助于执行主要任务 - 将火力集中在 c 线上。

zh: 白方已经得到了他想要的一切：占领空位并侵入对手阵营；入侵象至第六级；抓住他的作品的中心和和谐的动作。所有这些灾难都降临在黑方身上，都是由于第 13 步棋的严重计划错误造成的。

text: A very passive plan. White simply develops his pieces without thinking a about countering the main link in Black's plan - the advance... e5. His task would undoubtedly be made difficult if White were to play now Bf4 or Bg5. It is unfavourable for Black to win back the pawn 7... Qa5+ 8
zh: 一个非常被动的计划。白方只是简单地发展他的棋子，而没有考虑对抗黑方计划中的主要环节——前进……e5。如果白方现在下Bf4或Bg5，他的任务无疑会变得困难。不利于黑方夺回棋子 7... Qa5+ 8

text: Naturally! The pawn sacrifice has fully justified itself. Black now carries outhe advance of the e-pawn without difficulty, while the bishops are placed on adjacent diagonals, where they will rake the centre and White's king's side castled position. After the march of the pawn... e5-e4, the knight f3 will have to look for another
zh: 当然！兵的牺牲已经完全证明了其合理性。现在，黑方可以毫无困难地推进e兵，而象则位于相邻的对角线上，他们将在那里掠夺中心和白方王方的易位后的王城。兵行军后...e5-e4，马f3将不得不寻找另一个

text: haven, after which the h2 and g2 points become real weaknesses. 8. Nc3 O-O 9. Be2 Bb7 10. b3 Nbd7 11. Bb2 Qe7 12. O-O Rad8
zh: 避风港，之后 h2 和 g2 点就成为真正的弱点。8. Nc3 O-O 9. Be2 Bb7 10. b3 Nbd7 11. Bb2 Qe7 12. O-O Rad8

zh: 不管笼罩在白方立场上的风暴有多么强大，他想要完全应对它是很难忍受的。塔拉什组织了一份精心策划的保卫王“堡垒”的计划。

zh: 进攻开始。威胁是... e4，随后对 h2 点进行攻击。为了保卫它，他需要转移马，

zh: 通过d2，到f1。首先他必须把车移开——但是移到哪里呢？只到e1，因为d1方，虽然在

text: an open file, must be occupied by the knight, in order to defend the f2s square which is dangerously weakened after the removal of the king's rook. And so White's immediate defensive operation consists

text: We refer to the pawn phalanx. This name is given to some (most frequently two) connected pawns, out of which at least one is situated on an open file. The phalanx - this is clearly dynamic, connected with forward movement. This sort of pawn-pair potentially has dynamic capable ofbreaking power, through the enemy front. The central phalanx with pawns on the d and c-files is a very active weapon. Often another phalanx is met in practice, made up of the e and f-pawns; we give it detailed consideration in the next chapter. Here, however, we stay with the basic aspect of the phalanx, consisting of the “"hanging" pawns, i.e. pawns which are situated on two open files and isolated from the rest of the pawn chain. Usually the "hanging" phalanx comes about on the c and d-files, since its formation for the most part is connected with definite opening systems and variations. We look at a few examples.

text: Here we have a position from the 19th game of the Tarrasch- Chigorin match of 1893.The White pawn on e4 is under attack. Black intends this planned objective, arising from the following considerations: the e4 pawn lacks pawn cover, it is also difficult to defend it with pieces, since White's king's bishop has been exchanged, while it is not so easy to mobilise his queen's rook; finally the central pawns are convenient targets for attack on the open lines - the e-file and the a8-h1 diagona1, which are in Black's hands. text: There is a quiet opening, where the first skirmish in the centre is a long time coming, and does not bring an advantage to either side. White begins the offensive first with the move f4, which had been tried time and again in practice and, up to this game, given good results for White. Even in the opening stage, Rubinstein thought out a plan of attack on the e4 square and foresaw that it would be weakened by the move f4. The attack launched by White looked dangerous, but required energetic and1 purposeful 1. execution. Duras was not able to permeate his play with concrete ideas, to map out a clear outline of the objective and a real way of achieving it. Separate passive moves began to interrupthe planned line of his thoughts, the attack came to assume a shapeless character, whereas Rubinstein continued purposefully f force to pressure on the e4 pawn. Soon this pressure was converted to an energetic attack by nearly all the Black pieces. The central stronghold of White's position - the e4 pawn fell, and this led to a disintegration of his king's flank.
